evidence_interpretation: Human OVOL2 expression was inversely associated with CDH2/N-cadherin in nasopharyngeal carcinoma; cross-species expression context only, not mouse direct-binding corroboration.
Independent mouse presomitic-mesoderm study reports the MSGN1/DLL3 regulatory program; added to the overlay as corroborating citation.
Independent mouse pancreatic study includes MIST1 binding and mutant-enhancer analysis at Rab26; useful mechanism context but not same-species human corroboration.
Existing second primary source supports the same mouse NOBOX/Pou5f1 relationship; no additional upgrade needed.
The located record is the existing GPS2/ABCA1 macrophage study, which provides ChIP, loss-of-function, expression, protein, and cholesterol-efflux evidence; no duplicate corroboration counted.
The strongest exact source is the existing YAP/TAZ study; combined YAP/TAZ evidence is retained as cofactor context and not recounted as independent YAP1-only corroboration.
Search result resolves to the existing ASH2L/ADAM17 study; no independent exact source was identified.
Full text confirms METTL3-dependent ADAM10 mRNA stabilization and perturbation, but the located record is the existing primary study, not independent corroboration.
Independent study reports inefficient Factor Xa cleavage of human CCN1 protein; this supports a separate proteolysis mechanism, not the promoted Factor Xa/PAR1 downstream-CCN1 RNA relay.

Independent COPD skeletal-muscle study links combined YAP/TAZ activity to ACTR2 expression and tests YAP-dependent ACTR2 promoter regulation; it is useful orthogonal context but does not establish a YAP1-only or same-species human edge.

Older macrophage corepressor work provides a distinct GPS2-NCoR/ABCA1 repression context, rather than the promoted LPS-induced GPS2/p65 activation mechanism; retain as a separate mechanism and do not count as exact corroboration.

AACR 2025 abstract reports STAG2 ChIP-seq/ChIP-qPCR, knockout, promoter acetylation, and ABCA1 expression in MIBC; the matching bioRxiv record appears to be the same study, so it is not independent corroboration.
